newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's secondary Cetes rates soar 295 bps.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's secondary Cetes rates soar 295 bps.

text.p: Overnight Cetes rates on Mexico's secondary money market rose 295 basis points to 24.25 percent on Friday in what dealers said was market speculation ahead of key elections on July 6.
"Rates have gone up sharply, but it is pure speculation. Big players are hiding money," one dealer said.
In one trade, 200 million pesos were placed at 24.25 percent, one dealer said. Another trade for the same amount was made at 24.15 percent, he added.
One money market dealer said the market was showing jitters ahead of the vote next week and speculators were pushing up rates.
Mexico elects a new Congress, a quarter of the Senate, six govenors and the mayor of Mexico City on July 6.
